subject: Service remit approval: latency compensation proposal for Acme Health
messages:
From: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Elevated latency window this morning — what remediation/credits are available?

Hi Stephanie,

We're seeing repeated tail-latency spikes across our production workloads between 02:45–03:30 UTC this morning. End-user pages timed out and a handful of background jobs retried; I've pulled a quick CloudWatch trace and attached the timestamps. This aligns with increased error rates reported by our ops team.

Given the impact to our customers, we need to understand:
- Was this an internal Redwood incident or a customer-side misconfiguration?
- Can you share a timeline and remediation plan?
- What compensation or remediation does Redwood offer for SLA/latency breaches?

We're preparing a short post-mortem to share with the execs and will need any credits/offsets documented for our renewal discussions. Please flag urgent contacts if needed.

Thanks,
Jordan Hale
VP, Engineering — Acme Health
Acme Health

Attachment: cloudwatch-snippets-20261124.txt

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Acme DevOps <ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Elevated latency window this morning — what remediation/credits are available?

Hi Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the traces. I'm really sorry you hit that window. We've pulled the infra traces and are doing a deep-dive with runtime engineers now.

Immediate steps we're taking:
- Investigating kernel path and batching behavior that caused tail latency.
- Dropping a config patch to affected pool and monitoring for recurrence.
- Preparing an incident report and a short remediation timeline (ETA 24 hours).

For compensation, we typically handle SLO breaches with one-off account credits or pro-rated invoices depending on impact. I'll escalate for an exec approval for a concession (so you have something documented for renewals) and circle back with a concrete proposal in the next 48 hours.

Attachment: incident-report-20261124.pdf (preliminary)

Appreciate the patience — will follow up with specifics.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Elevated latency window this morning — request for documented concession (Acme Health)

Hi Marcus / Lauren — looping you in. Acme Health (RD-7341) experienced a tail-latency incident on 11/24 that impacted user traffic and background jobs. Jordan requested a documented remediation/credit for renewal talks. Preliminary incident report attached.

Customer impact (summary):
- Approx. 45 minutes of elevated p99 latency with intermittent 504s (their ops captured timeouts).
- Estimated visible user errors for a small percentage of active sessions during the window.
- Acme is sensitive due to an upcoming renewal in January.

Options I'm proposing for executive sign-off (pick one):
A) One-time account credit of $35,000 applied to next invoice — keeps accounting clean for renewal.
B) One waived invoice month (Nov invoice) equivalent to ~ $28,000 in committed spend + a $7,500 usage credit for good will.
C) Pro-rated credit tied to exact impacted token usage (administratively heavier; estimated ~$18k).

Rationale: we want to retain Acme and avoid escalation into procurement/discount cycles at renewal while staying within our internal credit policy. My recommendation is option A (single $35k credit) to simplify reconciliation and show meaningful remediation value.

Budget constraints: if we need to cap, I'd accept a $25k one-time credit as a manager-approved compromise. Please advise on which option you're comfortable approving and any additional legal/billing terms we should require (release language, one-time settlement).

Attachments: incident-report-20261124.pdf, billing-usage-export-Nov.csv

— Stephanie

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Elevated latency window this morning — request for documented concession (Acme Health)

Thanks Steph — reviewed the incident summary and the renewal sensitivity. I approve a one-time account credit up to $25,000 as a goodwill concession. Prefer to apply as an account-level credit on the next invoice and mark it ‘one-time goodwill, non-recurring’.

Please ensure:
- We confirm exact invoice mechanics with Billing (cc: billing) before sending to customer.
- The customer accepts the credit in writing (email is fine) and we add standard settlement language — "acceptance of credit constitutes full and final remedy for the incident" — to avoid future reopenings.
- Track this as an ARR-impacting concession in the renewal playbook so Sales Ops can flag at renewal.

If Stephanie wants to offer a waived invoice month instead of credit, that needs VP-level approval (not a manager). For speed, use the $25k credit.

— Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Enterprise
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Elevated latency window this morning — request for documented concession (Acme Health)

I've reviewed. Legal is fine with the credit as long as we get customer confirmation and include a short settlement paragraph in the email: 

"By accepting this account credit, Acme Health acknowledges that the credit is a one-time, non-recurring remedy for the specified service impact and does not constitute an admission of liability beyond the agreed SLO terms."

Also recommend we copy Finance/Billing and include the billing export (attached) so the applied credit posts cleanly. Once you have Jordan's OK, cc me and I'll sign the settlement language.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Acme DevOps <ops@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Billing <billing@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Resolution: one-time account credit for 11/24 latency window (RD-7341)

Hi Jordan — quick follow-up with an approved remediation plan. Thanks again for the patience while we investigated.

Summary of remedy:
- Redwood will apply a one-time account credit of $25,000 to Acme Health’s next invoice (non-recurring).
- Credit will be processed by Billing and should appear on your December invoice; attached is the usage export to assist reconciliation.
- Legal has requested a brief confirmation sentence for closure. Please reply to this thread with the single sentence below if you accept the credit: 

"Acme Health accepts the one-time account credit of $25,000 as full and final remedy for the Redwoods service impact on 2026-11-24."

Once we receive that reply we'll route to Billing and mark the case closed on our side. If you'd prefer alternate mechanics (waived invoice month), we can escalate to VP for further approval, but for speed we suggest the credit.

Attachment: billing-usage-export-Nov.csv

Apologies again for the disruption — we've put a runtime mitigation in place and will share the full post-mortem by end of day Monday.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134
